name: Spain
note: A death becomes known to the state through the Civil Registry: the hospital where it occurs must send the official form and the medical certificate electronically to the Registry and to the National Statistics Institute, and no death can be registered without that certificate. Registration authorises burial or cremation unless a court must intervene. From the Registry the death flows on its own to the INE and the municipal population registers, to the electoral census, and to any administration that reads the single electronic register. Families still have to obtain certificates of last wills and of life insurance policies themselves, fifteen days after the death.

steps.title: Doctor confirms the death and sends the parte de defunción
steps.who: The doctor who attended the deceased in the last illness, or any doctor who examines the body.
steps.summary: The doctor records the unmistakable signs of death, its cause, and the date, time and place, and sends the report to the Civil Registry at once. Where a Civil Registry doctor (Médico del Registro Civil) is attached to the office, that doctor checks the report by examining the body.

steps.title: Medical certificate of death is a precondition of registration
steps.summary: No death can be registered without the medical certificate. Besides the registration particulars it records what the National Statistics Institute needs and whether there are signs of violent death or judicial proceedings; those items are not entered in the register.

steps.title: Signs of violent death are referred to the judicial authority
steps.who: The certifying doctor, and the Registry officer (Encargado), who is told urgently; the competent court (juzgado) decides.
steps.trigger: Signs of violent death, or any case where judicial proceedings must be opened.
steps.summary: Signs of violent death are reported urgently to the Registry officer. Registration can still proceed, but it does not by itself authorise burial or cremation: the licence issues only when the competent court authorises it.

steps.title: Hospital sends the death form and certificate electronically
steps.localName: comunicación de la defunción por los centros sanitarios
steps.who: The management of the hospital, clinic or health establishment where the death occurred (first in the statutory order of persons obliged to promote registration).
steps.trigger: A death in a health establishment.

deadline.text: within the period set by regulation; the 1958 Regulation still requires the checks and burial licence within 24 hours of the death

steps.summary: Hospital staff send the completed official form and the signed medical certificate electronically, using secure electronic identification and signature, to the competent Civil Registry office.

steps.title: Deaths outside a health establishment are declared through the public authority
steps.who: In order: the doctor who certified the death outside a health establishment; the relatives or someone they authorise; the head of the establishment, anyone living in the house, or the relevant authority. Under the 1958 Regulation the duty to declare extends to blood relatives to the fourth degree and in-laws to the second.
steps.trigger: A death outside a health establishment.

deadline.text: as soon as possible; the authority passes it on immediately

steps.summary: The persons obliged to promote registration inform the public authority as soon as possible, and the authority communicates the death immediately to the Civil Registry office.

steps.title: Registry officer registers the death and issues the burial or cremation licence
steps.localName: inscripción de la defunción; licencia de entierro
steps.trigger: Receipt of the official form with the medical certificate.

deadline.text: registration immediately on receipt; checks and burial licence within 24 hours of the death

steps.summary: Registration of every death is compulsory. The officer registers the death at once, issues the death certificate, and then issues the licence for burial or cremation. Registration closes the person's individual record.

steps.title: Death certificates are issued from the single electronic register
steps.who: The person concerned, or anyone else who identifies themselves and shows a legitimate interest.
steps.summary: The Civil Registry is public, but certificates about another person go only to an identified applicant with a legitimate interest. Certificates are issued electronically as a rule.

steps.title: Certificate of last wills from the General Register of Last Wills
steps.who: Anyone who proves the death with an authentic document; the register is the Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad of the Ministry of Justice.

deadline.text: not before fifteen days after the death

steps.summary: The register states whether any will or other act of last will is recorded for the deceased, so that heirs can find the notary who holds it.

steps.title: Hospitals report each death to the National Statistics Institute
steps.who: The management of the health establishment.
steps.trigger: A death in a health establishment.
steps.summary: The same electronic communication that goes to the Civil Registry goes to the Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE).

steps.title: Civil Registry offices send deaths to the INE for the municipal registers
steps.who: Civil Registry offices, sending through the INE.
steps.summary: Civil Registry offices must send births, deaths and changes of name, sex and nationality to each municipality through the INE, at least monthly.

steps.title: INE passes the deaths to the municipality, which updates the Padrón
steps.who: The INE, on behalf of the central administration bodies.
steps.summary: State bodies send each municipality the changes to its residents' data so that the municipal population register (Padrón) stays current.

steps.title: Civil Registry tells the Electoral Census Office
steps.trigger: Any change affecting entries in the electoral census.
steps.summary: Registry officers report monthly to the provincial delegations of the Oficina del Censo Electoral any circumstance affecting the census, which includes deaths.

steps.title: Public administrations read the Civil Registry directly
steps.who: Every public administration and official, within its competence; periodic automated feeds can be agreed for public purposes.
steps.trigger: A need for the data in the exercise of a public function.
steps.summary: All administrations have electronic access to the single Civil Registry, and the Directorate General can set up periodic automated supply for public purposes. Administrations may not ask citizens for a certificate they can obtain electronically.

steps.title: Ministry of Justice supplies Civil Registry data to the Social Security bodies
steps.who: The body designated by the Ministry of Justice, to the Social Security managing bodies (INSS and others).
steps.trigger: A request from the Social Security body.
steps.summary: The Ministry of Justice must give the Social Security managing bodies the registry information they request that bears on the start, change or end of benefit entitlement.

steps.title: Insurers report every life policy to the register of death-cover insurance
steps.localName: Registro de contratos de seguros de cobertura de fallecimiento
steps.who: Insurers writing life or accident policies with death cover; the register is kept by the Registro General de Actos de Última Voluntad.
steps.summary: Insurers must report the insured person, the insurer and the policy, and must report when a benefit has been paid. Non-compliance is an administrative infringement under insurance supervision law.

steps.title: Anyone with the death certificate can ask which insurers covered the deceased
steps.localName: certificado de contratos de seguros de cobertura de fallecimiento
steps.who: Any interested person, presenting the death certificate.

deadline.text: not before fifteen days after the death

steps.summary: The register issues a certificate listing the policies in force and the insurers. The data stay available for five years.

steps.title: The enquirer asks the insurer whether they are a beneficiary
steps.who: The holder of the register certificate.
steps.summary: With the certificate, the enquirer can ask each insurer whether they are a beneficiary; a non-beneficiary is told only that.

steps.title: Notaries handling an inheritance must obtain the insurance register certificate
steps.who: Notaries asked to authorise the allocation or partition of inherited property.
steps.summary: The notary requests the certificate electronically unless the parties provide it, incorporates it in the deed, and warns the parties if a death-cover policy exists.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: The 2011 Act sets no fixed number of days: hospitals must report electronically within a period set by regulation. The 1958 Regulation, still applied, requires the registration checks and burial licence within 24 hours of the death.

informantDuty.note: The hospital or health establishment is first in the statutory order and reports electronically; then the doctor (deaths outside a facility), the relatives, and others.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of every certificate. Under the 1958 Regulation a Médico del Registro Civil, where one is attached to the office, checks the doctor's report by examining the body.

electronicRegistration.note: Health establishments must send the form and certificate electronically; deaths elsewhere are reported through the public authority.

centralPopulationRegister.name: Padrón municipal (municipal registers coordinated by the INE)
centralPopulationRegister.note: No single central population register: each municipality keeps its Padrón, coordinated by the INE. The Civil Registry itself is now a single electronic register.

governmentPropagation.note: Registration feeds the INE and the municipal Padrón (at least monthly) and the electoral census (monthly); administrations can read the register electronically, and Social Security receives registry data on request.

certificateAccess.note: The register is public, but information about another person goes only to an identified applicant with a legitimate interest.

privateSectorVerification.note: No general death feed for banks. The death-cover insurance register is a sector-specific official route, but it is queried by the family with the death certificate, not by insurers checking deaths.

gaps: The 24-hour deadline for hospitals' electronic communication was not found in Ley 20/2011, which leaves the period to regulation; the deadline recorded is from the 1958 Regulation (art. 276), still applied in what is compatible with the 2011 Act. No new Civil Registry regulation was located.

No legal provision was found that pushes deaths automatically from the Civil Registry to the INSS, the Agencia Tributaria or the DNI/passport authority; LGSS art. 71.1.b provides supply on request only. Any automated daily feed rests on agreements not located.
No rule found obliging banks to check deaths, and no official death-verification service for banks; the family presents the death certificate.
No statutory public-notice (edicto) step on death was identified; inheritance edicts arise only in specific succession procedures not researched here.
The relationship between the 1958 Reglamento and Ley 20/2011 (transitional application) was not confirmed from the transitional provisions' text.
